shared_conventions:
Verified by running `opencli --help`, `opencli list --help`, `opencli list -f yaml`, and `opencli <site> --help -f yaml` for all eight sites (v1.8.6, node v22.23.1; binary is a symlink: /Users/donghanglyu/.local/bin/opencli -> ../lib/node_modules/@jackwener/opencli/dist/src/main.js).

COMMON OPTIONS (identical block emitted by all 8 adapters):
- `-f, --format <fmt>` — choices table|plain|json|yaml|md|csv, default `table`. Per-COMMAND help additionally emits an `output_formats` list (table, plain, yaml, json, md, csv) that the per-SITE help omits.
- `--trace <mode>` — choices off|on|retain-on-failure, default `off`.
- `-v, --verbose` — Debug output, default false.
- `-h, --help`.
Global (from `opencli --help`): `--profile <name>` — "Chrome profile/context alias for Browser Bridge commands"; `-V, --version`.

BROWSER COMMON OPTIONS (attached only to commands with `browser: true`):
- `--window <mode>` — foreground|background. I used `--window background` on both browser probes and neither opened a visible window.
- `--site-session <mode>` — ephemeral|persistent. Adapter site session lifecycle.
- `--keep-tab <bool>` — true|false. Keep the browser tab lease after the command finishes.
Commands with `browser: false` (nowcoder companies/creators/hot/jobs/recommend/topics/trending; 1point3acres digest/forum/forums/hot/latest/thread/user) do NOT receive these three flags at all.

MACHINE-READABLE CONTRACT: `opencli <site> --help -f yaml` returns site, command_count, and per command: name, command, usage, access, description, browser, domain, positionals[], command_options[] (name/type/default/required/choices/help), columns[], example, and sometimes siteSession. Every adapter ends with a `next:` block listing `opencli <site> <command> --help -f yaml`. `columns` is the authoritative output-field list and matched the real JSON keys exactly on both probes.

`access` FIELD is the read/write safety marker on every command — read | write. I honored this and ran zero write commands.

`opencli list -f yaml` (1275 command entries total across all adapters) carries TWO fields the per-site help does not expose:
- `strategy` — across the whole install the distinct values are: cookie, intercept, local, public, ui. For the 8 job sites only public / cookie / ui appear. public ⇔ browser:false (direct HTTP); cookie ⇔ browser:true using session cookies; ui ⇔ browser:true driving the DOM (all LinkedIn salesnav-*, thread-snapshot, sent-invitations, connect, safe-send).
- `aliases` — only three exist among these 8 sites: indeed job → [detail, view]; upwork detail → [job, view]; upwork feed → [best-matches].

EXIT CODES / ERROR SURFACE (observed): success → JSON array on stdout, empty stderr, exit 0 (51job and indeed probes). Failure → exit 1, NOTHING on stdout, and a YAML block on STDERR even when `-f json` was requested:
  ok: false
  error:
    code: COMMAND_EXEC
    message: '<site> request failed: HTTP 403 Forbidden from <url>'
    exitCode: 1
So a caller parsing stdout as JSON must check the exit code — a failure yields empty stdout, not a JSON error object, and the error dialect is YAML regardless of -f.

AUTH: `opencli auth status` supports --site <comma-list>, --full, --concurrency <n>, --timeout <seconds>, --only all|logged-in|not-logged-in|unknown|error, -f. Row shape: site, status, logged_in, identity, checked, error. `checked` is "quick" | "full" | "skipped". `opencli auth refresh` also exists ("Touch logged-in site sessions to keep browser auth fresh") — not run. Adapters with an auth adapter expose `login` (write) + `whoami` (read), both with siteSession: persistent.

BROWSER BRIDGE HEALTH: `opencli doctor` → "[OK] Daemon: running on port 19825 (v1.8.6) / [OK] Extension: connected (v1.0.22) / Profiles: • n4drczmg: connected v1.0.22 / [OK] Connectivity: connected in 2.1s / Everything looks good!"

Raw captures saved at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-donghanglyu/d1ca171b-6798-42dc-9582-87e4635be401/scratchpad/ — help_{linkedin,indeed,51job,nowcoder,1point3acres,upwork,maimai}.yaml, list_all.yaml, probe_{51job,indeed,1p3a}.{json,err}, extract.py.

failure_modes.detection: Exit code 1. stdout EMPTY. stderr carries YAML: `ok: false` / `error.code: COMMAND_EXEC` / `error.message: '1point3acres request failed: HTTP 403 Forbidden from https://www.1point3acres.com/bbs/forum-145-1.html'` / `error.exitCode: 1`. Detect on exit!=0 first, then parse stderr as YAML and read error.code + error.message; do NOT try to parse stdout as JSON.
failure_modes.right_response: Cross-check with `opencli auth status --site <site> -f json`. If not_logged_in, the fix is `opencli <site> login` — a WRITE command, so surface it to the user rather than running it. Do not retry the read: the 403 is deterministic while logged out. Critically, do not trust `strategy: public` / `browser: false` as evidence that no login is needed — 1point3acres forum is public-strategy and still 403s.

failure_modes.mode: Silent partial extraction — exit 0, rows returned, documented columns empty (OBSERVED on indeed)
failure_modes.detection: Exit 0 and a well-formed JSON array, so every status check passes. The defect is only visible by inspecting VALUES: `opencli indeed search "mri" --limit 2` returned 2 rows where title, salary and tags were all empty strings while id/company/location/url were populated. Detect by asserting that the identifying field (title) is non-empty on the returned rows, not by checking the exit code.
failure_modes.right_response: Treat a search row as untrusted until a key field is confirmed non-empty. For indeed, follow each `id` with `opencli indeed job <id>` to recover the title. Report the gap rather than presenting empty titles as 'no data'. Never infer 'the site has no such jobs' from blank fields — the rows existed.

failure_modes.mode: Login state reported as `unknown` rather than a boolean (OBSERVED on nowcoder, maimai, and ~15 other sites)
failure_modes.detection: `opencli auth status -f json` row reads status "unknown", logged_in "" (empty string, NOT false), checked "skipped", error "quickCheck not implemented; use --full to run whoami". A caller doing `if (!row.logged_in)` will silently misread this as logged-out.
failure_modes.right_response: Re-probe with `opencli auth status --site <sites> --full --timeout 40 -f json`, which runs the read-only `whoami` and returns checked:"full". I did exactly this for nowcoder/maimai/1point3acres/upwork and all four resolved to not_logged_in. Distinguish the three states (logged_in / not_logged_in / unknown) explicitly; never collapse unknown into false.

failure_modes.mode: Site has no auth adapter at all (OBSERVED for indeed and 51job)
failure_modes.detection: The site is simply ABSENT from `opencli auth status -f json` — the call returned 65 rows and grep for indeed/51job matched none, while the other six target sites were all present. Confirmed independently: neither adapter's yaml help lists a `login` or `whoami` command. This is different from not_logged_in and different from unknown.
failure_modes.right_response: Read it as 'no login concept for this adapter', not as an error or a missing adapter. These are the sites to reach for first when no session is available — 51job in particular worked immediately and completely. Do not attempt `opencli 51job login`; the command does not exist.

failure_modes.mode: Browser bridge unavailable — daemon down or extension disconnected
failure_modes.detection: NOT OBSERVED IN THIS SESSION, so the exact failure text is unverified. What I can source: `opencli doctor` is the designated diagnostic and prints per-component lines that were all `[OK]` here — 'Daemon: running on port 19825 (v1.8.6)', 'Extension: connected (v1.0.22)', 'Connectivity: connected in 2.1s'. Any browser:true command depends on all three. `opencli daemon status|restart|stop` exists per `opencli --help`.
failure_modes.right_response: Run `opencli doctor` before concluding a site adapter is broken, since a dead bridge would take out every browser:true command across all sites at once — a useful signal to distinguish infrastructure failure from a single-site problem. The strategy=public / browser=false commands (nowcoder companies/jobs/hot/topics/trending/recommend/creators; 1point3acres forum/thread/hot/latest/digest/forums/user) should be unaffected by a bridge outage. I did not induce this failure, so treat the detection string as unconfirmed.

failure_modes.detection: NOT OBSERVED — neither probe returned an empty array, so I cannot report what a genuine zero-result response looks like (empty JSON array `[]` on exit 0 is the plausible shape but I did not see it). The important hazard is the ambiguity: a 403 gives exit 1 + empty stdout, which a naive `JSON.parse(stdout || '[]')` would convert into a zero-result success.
failure_modes.right_response: Always branch on exit code before interpreting emptiness. Only call something 'no results' when exit==0 AND stdout parsed to an array; if exit!=0, it is a failure regardless of how empty stdout looks.

failure_modes.detection: NOT OBSERVED. I have no evidence of a risk-control or CAPTCHA failure mode in this toolset and cannot state how one would surface. Listed only so it is not mistaken for something I checked.
failure_modes.right_response: If encountered, capture the raw stderr and re-run `opencli doctor`; do not assume it resembles the 403 shape above. Use `--trace on` (a documented common option) to capture a trace for diagnosis.
